**Left alone deliberately, and now written down.** The low-level `SymbolRenderer.Render(canvas, area, …)` and `SKCanvas.Render` overloads for the square symbologies still fill the area they are given, so a caller who wants pre-distorted modules (an output device whose dot pitch differs by axis is the one real use case anyone could name) still has a way to draw them. Reviewing the result found that only the rMQR overload said anything about stretching, so the escape hatch was indistinguishable from an oversight; both types now carry the rule, the threshold it fails at, and the reason rMQR differs, in their XML docs.

**Follow-up, its own PR.** The asymmetry itself stands. It is F1 in the Follow-ups table above, with the resolution recorded in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) as well, since that survives this plan.

### Adversarial review of the canvas fit (2026-09-10)

**Five lenses in parallel, then three refuters on the one claim that changed code.** The claim was mine and it was a regression: single-precision `matrixSize * (canvas / matrixSize)` can land a hair above the canvas, so the centering offset comes back about 1.5e-5 low, and flooring it loses a whole pixel. Unanimous (3/3 not refuted), reproduced independently by a fourth agent measuring performance, and visible in the SVG output as `<rect fill="white" x="-1" y="-1" width="450" height="450"/>`. On a square canvas the symbol fits exactly, so that -1 opened a one-pixel band of pad along the far edges of an image that should have none, shifted the symbol up and left, and flipped `ContentCoversCanvas`, which cost the opaque surface. Invisible with the default colours, because the pad is then the background beside it; a distinct `clearColor` shows it, and 4 to 5.5 % of (version, canvas) pairs are affected. Not present at `5b8a3a1`: the square symbologies did not reach the letterbox path before this change.

**The first fix was wrong, in the way half-fixes usually are.** Clamping the offset at zero rescued the case where the true offset *is* zero and left every other integer offset one pixel low, so a canvas whose leftover divides evenly came out with bands 2 px apart (a 45-module symbol at 200x400 gave 99 and 101). The round-two reviewer found it by attacking the fix rather than the original defect. What the arithmetic needs is not a clamp but slack: the offset absorbs 1e-3 before flooring, which is orders of magnitude above the error and below anything a viewer could see. Three test helpers had copied the pre-fix formula and had to follow, or they would describe a grid the builder no longer draws on.

**Every number the change published was wrong.** The 1.67:1 and 1.25:1 thresholds came from one symbol, one styling and one orientation. Re-measured across three symbols (two of 33 modules, one of 45), four styles and both orientations, failures appear from about 1.25:1 and nothing survives past about 1.8:1 — the styled limit is 1.67:1 with a different payload of the same module count, portrait fails at about 1.40:1 for everything, and ZXing disagrees with this library in both directions rather than agreeing with it. "In our decoder and in ZXing alike" was false. The docs now state the range and say plainly that there is no threshold worth aiming at, which is the more useful claim anyway.

**The migration guide's own escape hatch was broken, and three reviewers found it independently.** `SKCanvas.Render` clears the whole canvas itself, so the `Clear(SKColors.White)` the guide put in front of it was dead code and the recommended replacement produced a half-transparent image — the exact failure the next section of the same guide is about. Also corrected there: the 2.0.0 opener and the summary table both said the release was renames and `using` lines, with three behaviour sections below them; "`WithModulePixelSize` is unaffected" contradicted the padding section twelve lines later; and the non-square warning added to `SymbolRenderer` and `SKCanvasExtensions` sat on the type, where C# tooling never shows it, rather than on the members.

**Mutation testing found what the new suite could not see.** Removing `Math.Floor`, dropping half of the too-small-canvas guard, and collapsing the opacity decision to the pad colour all left the single-framework suite green. Those three now have cases, as do a translucent `clearColor`, a clear colour showing through a transparent background, and the three pad bands nothing had ever sampled. A third round found two more: the single-coat rule was pinned only on a letterbox pad, which is two bands with no corner, so a mutant widening the side bands over the corners survived; and nothing bounded the epsilon from above, so 1e-2 passed although it is past the geometric margin. That margin is now measured rather than assumed, and a PR review found the first attempt at measuring it wrong. The bound was stated for a 159-module matrix, which is what the builder's own `WithQuietZone` can reach — but the generator options and the data constructors cap the quiet zone at 10,000 rather than 10, so a caller can build a 20,000-module matrix through ordinary public API, and the closest a real offset can then sit below a whole pixel is 2.5e-5 rather than 2.5e-3. An exact-integer oracle found the consequence: `RmQRCodeData(R7x139, 195)` on a 533x402 canvas has an exact offset of 1057/1058, which 1e-3 rounded up to a whole pixel. Only a rectangular matrix can do this, since a square one puts both offsets on halves. The fix is to compute the fit in double rather than read it back from the renderer's float rectangle: that drops the arithmetic error to about 1e-10, five orders of magnitude under the tightest geometric bound, so an epsilon of 1e-6 separates the two at every matrix size the data types accept. The Debug suite went from 18,083 cases to 18,113.

**Benchmarks: the old note was true and worthless.** Every case in `QRCodeImageEndToEnd` uses a square canvas, so `FillAround` never ran and the opacity decision never differed; "unchanged" measured nothing. Two cases were added for the shapes that do exercise it, and on those the change is a win: a pad that used to be transparent now makes the surface opaque, measured at -29 % wall clock for `WithModulePixelSize(8) + WithSize(400, 400)`.

**Two follow-ups came out of the round, both recorded in the Follow-ups table.** F1 is the low-level renderer asymmetry. F2 came from the API lens noticing that the padding section walks readers into `WithColors` resetting the colours they had already set; a survey of four other libraries found none that asks a caller to choose between override and merge, so the answer is the single-colour setters they all provide rather than a semantics change to `WithColors`. Both are additive or separable, and neither blocks 2.0.0.

**Lessons.** A fix deserves the same adversarial attention as the defect: the clamp looked obviously right, passed the four tests written for the original symptom, and was wrong for every other value of the same variable. A measured number is a measurement of what you measured — one symbol, one orientation — and publishing it as a threshold invites someone to design against it; state the range and the conditions, or say there is no number. And "Historical" in a comment is a claim worth checking: this one meant a 2019 expression that nobody revisited, not a decision anyone would defend, and reading the first commit settled in minutes what the comment had protected for years. A test that pins a call's *shape* pins nothing about its behaviour — `WithSize_CustomSize_GeneratesCorrectSize` asserted the output was 300x400 and passed both before and after a change that altered every pixel in it, while the suite's silence about `WithSize(900, 450)` was itself the evidence, since the one test that touched that canvas asserted module centres and pointedly not that it decodes.

### The low-level renderer fits its area (2026-09-11)

**The last supported call that stretched a symbol is gone.** `SymbolRenderer.Render` and the `SKCanvas.Render` extensions for Standard QR and Micro QR now draw the symbol at one uniform module scale, centered in the area, with the background over the whole area, as rMQR's overload always has. The public `GetFinderPatternRect` and `GetIconRects` fit the same way, since a caller hands them the area they passed to `Render`. Everything below the fit was already per-axis (each draw routine divides the area's width and height independently), so the change is one rectangle computed once and passed where the area used to go; only the background keeps the caller's area. Measured before and after with this library's decoder: a 900x450 area (Standard and Micro QR) and a 200x280 portrait slot with circle modules and an icon did not decode and now do, 512x480 decodes both ways with different pixels, and a square area is pixel-identical.

**Checking the plan's order removed half of it.** F1 said the builders needed an axis-aware module size first, because fitting the renderer would remove the only way to pre-distort a symbol for an output device whose dots are not square. It would not: a 2:1 canvas scale over a square area reproduces the old fill with 0 differing pixels at 900x450, 600x400, 512x480 and 300x700 for plain modules and finders in a solid colour (styled output is drawn in the square and stretched with it, so it can differ), and a square area passes through the fit unchanged, so the escape hatch was never the stretched area. The use case itself was named in the #400 review to justify keeping the fill and has no report behind it, so `WithModulePixelSize(x, y)` waits for a request (F1). Found while checking, for whoever builds it: the anisotropy has to be a canvas transform over square cells. Handing the renderer a non-square content rectangle no longer does anything, since the renderer fits it to a square, and a path that skipped the fit to draw non-square cells would still get styled modules wrong: `CircleModuleShape` sizes its dot from the shorter side of the cell (with the old fill, 4x8 px of ink in an 8x8 cell after a simulated 2:1 playback, against 8x8 through the transform), and the rounded shapes take their corner radius from that side, so their corners come out uneven.

**The fit is the square on the shorter side, with slack for float rounding.** `GetLetterboxedArea` computes `n * (side / n)`, which in single precision need not give back `side`, so the square symbologies take the centered square on the shorter side instead. Comparing the sides exactly was the first version, and it was right only at integer coordinates: `SKRect.Create(x, y, s, s)` stores right and bottom as rounded sums, so a square at fractional coordinates comes out a float step from square in over half of random cases, and shrinking it by that step moved module edges by a pixel at some offsets and made fitting depend on how often it ran. An area square to within 1e-6 of its largest coordinate therefore comes back as given. That keeps every square render identical (the golden-pixel tests did not move) and makes fitting twice the same as fitting once, which the helpers rely on: the renderer hands them the area it already fitted, a caller hands them the original, and both get the same rectangle. The slack is measured from the largest absolute coordinate, so squares near the origin and at negative coordinates, where a translated canvas puts them, behave the same. An inverted area (a negative width or height) is refused with `ArgumentException` in all three symbologies, and so is a non-finite one; the extensions check before they clear the canvas. The first cut had pushed an inverted area 15,000 to 20,000 pixels outside a 400x200 area through a plain `Math.Min` of the signed sides, the second mirrored it inside, as the area taken literally had, and rMQR, untouched by either, still drew 15,077 pixels outside an area inverted vertically. Refusing it is the answer that holds: an inverted rect reads two ways, a mirror or the same bounds written backwards, and for an asymmetric symbol those are different pictures. Skia sorting an inverted rect before filling it is no guide, since a filled rect looks the same either way. The one real use behind the mirror reading, a transfer print or a sticker read through glass, is a canvas scale of -1 about the area, which all three symbologies' decoders read back. A zero-size area draws nothing rather than throwing, because a canvas before layout or a collapsed panel produces one routinely and a paint callback gains nothing from an exception. rMQR keeps `GetLetterboxedArea` as it was.

**Tests.** `SymbolRendererAreaFitTest`, 103 cases per framework. Decode through all three entry points (renderer, area extension, size extension) for Standard and Micro QR at 900x450, 300x900 and 600x400, with rMQR as the reference; 600x400 decoded even when stretched, so that row pins that a readable canvas stays readable rather than catching a lost fit. A grid-free check that the dark modules span a square centred in the area, and the background over the whole area and nothing outside it. Every draw path compared pixel for pixel with the same symbol drawn into its fitted square: circle modules, gaps, a circle finder, a gradient, and a translucent background with a finder shape for the layer path, because the plain case alone let five mutants through that each drew a styled symbol stretched. The extensions compared byte for byte, in order, with the renderer; an order-insensitive `IsEquivalentTo` on the image bytes had been blind to placement and took minutes per case. Inverted and non-finite areas refused by all three symbologies through the renderer, both helpers and the extensions (before the canvas is cleared, and a negative size on the width/height overloads); a zero-size area drawing nothing; and a -1 canvas scale about the area mirroring the upright render exactly. `GetFinderPatternRect` outlining the drawn finder and `GetIconRects` square and centred for module and percent sizing. `GetSquareArea` over 1,500 seeded fractional squares (ordinary, near the origin, negative), 1,000 fractional rectangles for idempotence and helper agreement, and three areas more than rounding from square, one of them a hundredth of a pixel off at a large offset, that must still be fitted, so a looser tolerance cannot bring the stretch back unnoticed. 28 of the first 40 cases failed before the change; the other 63 were added for the defects and surviving mutants found after it, and for refusing inverted areas. In `StyledSymbolDecodabilityTest`, `DecorativeFinder_NonSquareRect_RingsFollowTheGrid` draws each finder shape straight into a non-square rect, the only path left that produces one, and three comments that still described builder canvases as non-square now say what they test. Full suite green on both frameworks, 18,335 cases in Debug (17,961 passed, 374 skipped for unavailable SIMD paths).

**Docs say what was measured, and the migration images check it.** The generator made its stretched "before" image through the fill; it now asks for the stretch with a canvas scale over a square area, which gives the old fill's pixels exactly for plain modules in a solid colour, and regenerating left the existing images byte-identical. The guide's renderer section shows the renderer's own use rather than repeating the 900x450 banner: a 200x300 slot on a 280x380 card, stretched before (this library's decoder misses it; ZXing.Net and zxing-cpp read it) and fitted after (all three read it). The captions used to say no reader finds the stretched images, which zxing-cpp contradicts for both, so each caption now names the readers and the generator checks all three against it. Around the change, the `clearColor` docs on the extensions now say the background covers the area and the clear colour shows inside it only through a translucent background, `IconData`'s percent sizing is a percentage of the symbol's side, the per-symbology spec pages link to the measurements in `qrcode-symbologies.md` instead of restating them, and the Playground's API page is regenerated.

**Benchmarks: allocation identical, time inside the noise.** `QRCodeImageEndToEnd` and `MicroQRImageEndToEnd` against a worktree at `main`, ShortRun, run back to back after the final change: allocation identical to the byte on all twelve cases, and the largest mean increase +7.8 % on `M4_ImageDecode_Span`, a decode case the change does not touch (Small_512px 4.59 → 4.79 ms, Small_NonSquare_900x450 7.16 → 7.51, Large_512px 9.43 → 9.22, M4_512px 5.12 → 4.59). An earlier run had one row past +10 %, M4_128px at 323 → 373 us with a ±424 us error bar; re-measured alone with base and head alternating it came to +8.8 % and then +2 %. The fit is a handful of float operations per render and nothing in the per-module loops; ShortRun on this machine cannot resolve a few percent either way.

**Lessons.** An escape hatch recorded in review deserves the check a defect gets: this one was written down as the only route, and one canvas transform showed it was not needed, which turned a two-part PR with a new public API into a fit and the two helpers that follow it. A claim about pixels or readers is a claim about every case it does not exclude: "bit for bit" had been tested only at integer coordinates, "no reader finds it" only with this library's decoder, and "pixel for pixel" with plain modules, and each broke on the first case outside what was measured. Listing exceptions one at a time kept leaking new ones (circle finders, diagonal gradients, caption icons); saying what is exact and calling the rest different is what held. And a number restated on a second page drifts from the first: the Micro QR spec map had picked up a reader that cannot read Micro QR, so it now links to the one place the measurements live.
